assertion_analysis.assertions: test_a_clean_unrequested_exit_is_restarted: holder alive and eventually two starts
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Restore exec of the reader as batch process, or remove its restart loop.

assertion_analysis.assertions: test_stop_marks_retirement_but_reload_does_not: reload true, callback invoked, no stop file, stop false and marker file
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Reload becomes a stop, exec is withheld, or stop omits its lifetime marker.

assertion_analysis.assertions: test_deliberate_retirement_exits_the_holder: exit zero and no restart message
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Ignore the stop marker or restart after explicit retirement.
Omit active-marker recognition and restart a promoted holder with --standby.
Hardcode the current defaults rather than reading owner constants; does not fail on an independent change to next_backoff transition semantics.

assertion_analysis.assertions: scheduler job numeric and before_queue RUNNING; kill acknowledged
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Submission is malformed, job never reaches RUNNING, or kill handshake is absent.

assertion_analysis.assertions: thirty_second_queue RUNNING; survivors original PIDs true; explicit step State=RUNNING
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Restore Python-owned batch execution; negative-control-final.log fails on lost allocation.

assertion_analysis.assertions: at least two starts and restart elapsed below ten seconds
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Remove restart or increase its first delay beyond bound.

assertion_analysis.assertions: second descendant and step equal first
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Only if fixture stops copying original identity data; these assertions cannot independently detect product identity regression.

assertion_analysis.assertions: broken retry count 1..3, broken_queue RUNNING, unchanged Python starts
assertion_analysis.fails_if: Tight-loop retries, no retry, holder exits on exec failure, or decoy interpreter substitution never occurs.
Ignore retirement marker and hold allocation indefinitely.

findings.text: blocking: The generated shell independently implements steady-run reset, doubling and cap application already owned by reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:1036-1045 next_backoff; importing its three constants does not reuse its transition, so a change to the service policy can silently leave supervisor recovery on a different rule; derive the shell transition representation from that owner at submission time while preserving Python-independent execution.

non-blocking: Both PID equality assertions compare ready.json values with current.json values that the fixture copies directly from ready.json at lines 347-350; a session replacement that leaves those recorded IDs unchanged cannot redden them, so they are not independent identity coverage, although the original-PID liveness check at lines 253-257 independently protects survival.
